_meta.note: All values trace to evidence.csv rows. 'derived' = arithmetic on cited values; assumptions are named explicitly. No value was invented; where no verified observation exceeds the central value, high = central.

world_res_floor_added_m2_per_yr.basis: Central: UNEP/GlobalABC GSR 2025-2026 — residential stock floor area +3.4 bn m2 in 2024 (NET of demolitions; gross construction is somewhat higher, unquantified). Low: 3.4 bn minus the 2024->2025 fall in China developer residential completions (537.41 -> 428.30 mn m2, NBS) = 3.29 bn (assumes rest of world flat). High: 4.7 bn = all-building net additions (3.4 res + 1.3 non-res), i.e. current total building capacity if fully redirected to housing. Per capita today: 3.4e9 / 8.14e9 people = 418 m2 per 1000 people per yr.

max_build_rate_m2_per_1000people_per_yr.basis: Central/high: China 2011, newly built residential floor space urban 0.949 + rural 1.026 = 1.975 bn m2 (China Statistical Yearbook 2012 T10-35) / 1.345 bn people (World Bank) = 1,468 — highest verified national rate found; no verified observation above it, so high = central. Low: USA 2025 completions (1.005 m SF x 2,142 ft2 + 0.484 m MF x 1,000 ft2, Census medians) = 245 mn m2 / 340 m = 720. Comparators: EU27 2024 permits 362; China developers-only 2024 381; world 2024 418. Singapore HDB 1981-85 ~14.2 dwellings/1000/yr (unverified snippet; no m2 conversion).

labour_hours_per_m2.basis: Low: Finland 2023 precast apartments, 13 h per gross m2 across value chain (range 10-20; RT 2024). Central: China 2010 top-down — 41.60 m employed in construction enterprises / 2.7745 bn m2 completed (CSY 2011 T15-2) = 15.0 workers per 1,000 m2/yr x ASSUMED 2,200 h/yr = 33 h/m2 (biased up: enterprises also do civil works). High: India PMAY-G, 201 person-days per house (PIB 2025) / 25 m2 minimum size x ASSUMED 8 h/day = 64 h/m2 (biased up if houses > 25 m2).

cement_kg_per_m2.basis: Derived from residential concrete intensity (Heeren & Fishman 2019 MI database, residential n=455: Q1 303, median 613, Q3 974 kg/m2) x cement mass fraction of concrete ASSUMED 12.5% / 15% / 17% (typical 300-400 kg cement per ~2,400 kg m3; the '10-15% by volume' rule was seen only in search snippets — unverified). Excludes cement in mortar/plaster; the DB's separately reported 'cement' column has median 54 kg/m2 (n=148, IQR 14-151). Sample is Europe-heavy; brick/adobe-dominated South Asian and African housing may use less concrete.

steel_kg_per_m2.basis: Heeren & Fishman 2019 MI database, residential buildings n=431: Q1 10.9, median 26.7, Q3 59.0 kg per m2 gross floor area (computed from data/buildings.csv).

embodied_co2_kg_per_m2.basis: Life-cycle embodied carbon, EU residential: range 400-800, mean ~600 kgCO2e/m2 (Le Den, Röck et al. 2022, Ramboll/AAU/KU Leuven). Upfront (A1-A5) share ~2/3-70% => upfront ~270/400/560. Cross-check (derived): GSR 2.1 GtCO2/yr from cement, steel, aluminium in buildings / 4.7 bn m2 net added = ~447 kgCO2/m2 (materials only; numerator includes renovation, denominator is net).

supporting.world_construction_employment_basis: ILO Modelled Estimates (ILOSTAT SDMX), all construction; 8.26% of 3.56 bn employed. Southern Asia 91.6 m, Africa 24.8 m (SSA 15.3 m), Eastern Asia 75.2 m.
